```{python}
import polars as pl
from lets_plot import *
import requests
import io
import polars.selectors as cs

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)

# pull json data from https://github.com/byuidatascience/data4missing/raw/master/data-raw/flights_missing/flights_missing.json
response = requests.get("https://github.com/byuidatascience/data4missing/raw/master/data-raw/flights_missing/flights_missing.json")
df = pl.read_json(io.BytesIO(response.content))

```

```{python}
# Use cleaned data from Task 3 

nullified_df = df

# fix airport_code (!= 3 chars)
errors = df.filter(pl.col("airport_code").str.len_chars() != 3)
# print(errors) # There are 0 errors in "airport_code"

# fix airport_name (<4 chars)
errors = df.filter(pl.col("airport_name").str.len_chars() < 4)
# print(errors["airport_name"].unique()) # This prints out every unique value. In this case there are 56 instances of empty strings. 

nullified_df = nullified_df.with_columns(
    pl.when(pl.col("airport_name").str.len_chars() >= 4)
    .then(pl.col("airport_name"))
    .otherwise(None)
    .alias("airport_name")
)


# fix month (!= .isin(Jan-Dec))
months = ["January", "February", "Febuary", "March", "April", "May", "June", "July", "August", "September", "October", "November", "December"]
errors = df.filter(~pl.col("month").is_in(months))
# print(errors["month"].unique()) # Its just the misspelling of "February" and also "n/a"
# print(len(errors)) # 27 errors. (its "n/a")

nullified_df = nullified_df.with_columns(
    pl.when(pl.col("month").is_in(months))
    .then(pl.col("month"))
    .otherwise(None)
    .alias("month")
)

# if "num_of_delays_carrier" contains non numerical chars, convert to null
errors = df.filter(pl.col("num_of_delays_carrier").str.contains(r"[^0-9]"))
# print(errors["num_of_delays_carrier"].unique())
# print(len(errors)) # 73 instances of "1500+"

nullified_df = nullified_df.with_columns(
  pl.when(pl.col("num_of_delays_carrier") == "1500+")
  .then(None)
  .otherwise(pl.col("num_of_delays_carrier"))
  .alias("num_of_delays_carrier")
)


# Cast num_of_delays_carrier to i64
nullified_df = nullified_df.with_columns(
    pl.col("num_of_delays_carrier").cast(pl.Int64)
)

# Check all i64 columns for negative values, convert to null
columns_that_are_ints = nullified_df.select(cs.by_dtype(pl.Int64)).columns

nullified_df = nullified_df.with_columns(
     [
         pl.when(pl.col(col) < 0)
         .then(None)
         .otherwise(pl.col(col))
         .alias(col)
         for col in columns_that_are_ints
     ]
 )

cleaned_df = nullified_df

# Calculate medians for all 5 ints.
pl.col("minutes_delayed_carrier").fill_null(pl.col("minutes_delayed_carrier").median())

cleaned_df = cleaned_df.with_columns(
  pl.col("year").fill_null(pl.col("year").median())
)

cleaned_df = cleaned_df.with_columns(
  cs.starts_with("num_of_").fill_null(cs.starts_with("num_of_").median())
)

cleaned_df = cleaned_df.with_columns(
  cs.starts_with("minutes_").fill_null(cs.starts_with("minutes_").median())
)

df = cleaned_df

```

display(df)

Which delay is the worst delay? Keep working with the cleaned dataset you created in the previous task. Compare the proportion of flights delayed due to Carrier, to Security, and to Late Aircraft. Show this comparison in a Chart and a Table. 

The worst delay is due to late aircrafts which comes in at 31.94% of delays.

```{python}
'''
Todo:
- sum up each column
- get the grand total
- compute proportions for the 3 columns
- drop the unneeded columns
- display the table
- create a chart from the proportions
'''

Q1 = df.select(
    (pl.col("num_of_delays_carrier").sum()).alias("Carrier"),
    (pl.col("num_of_delays_security").sum()).alias("Security"),
    (pl.col("num_of_delays_late_aircraft").sum()).alias("Late Aircraft"),
    (pl.col("num_of_delays_total").sum()).alias("Grand_total")
).with_columns(
    (pl.col("Carrier") / pl.col("Grand_total")).alias("Carrier_Proportion"),
    (pl.col("Security") / pl.col("Grand_total")).alias("Security_Proportion"),
    (pl.col("Late Aircraft") / pl.col("Grand_total")).alias("Late_Aircraft_Proportion")
).drop("Carrier", "Security", "Late Aircraft", "Grand_total")

display(Q1)

# Now I'll unpivot it so I can make a nice bar chart
Q1_long = Q1.unpivot(
    on=["Late_Aircraft_Proportion", "Carrier_Proportion", "Security_Proportion"], # I put them in order here 
    variable_name="Delay_Type",
    value_name="Proportion"
)

# display(Q1_long)

(
    ggplot(data=Q1_long, mapping=aes(x="Delay_Type", y="Proportion"))
    + geom_bar(stat="identity")

    + theme_gray()
)

```


Create another chart that shows the proportion of delays for each reason (Carrier, Security, and Late Aircraft) across all 7 airports. 

The airport with the most security delays is SLC according to the data. The airport with the most carrier delays and the most amount of late aircraft delays is SAN. 

```{python}
"""
What I need: 
- 3 columns: airport_code, delay_Type, Proportion

Todo:
- research how to get 7 different charts in the same chart. 
     (I'm deffinitely doing stacked bar charts, looks cool)

- group by airport_code for airport isolation
- sum the 3 delay columns
- get grand total for each airport
- compute proportions per airport
- unpivot so each row is a delay type
- plot stacked bar chart (x=airport, x=proportion)
"""

display(df)

Q2_wide = df.group_by("airport_code").agg(
    pl.col("num_of_delays_carrier").sum(),
    pl.col("num_of_delays_security").sum(),
    pl.col("num_of_delays_late_aircraft").sum(),
    pl.col("num_of_delays_total").sum().alias("Grand_total")
).with_columns(
    (pl.col("num_of_delays_carrier") / pl.col("Grand_total")).alias("Carrier_Proportion"),
    (pl.col("num_of_delays_security") / pl.col("Grand_total")).alias("Security_Proportion"),
    (pl.col("num_of_delays_late_aircraft") / pl.col("Grand_total")).alias("Late_Aircraft_Proportion"),
).drop(
    "num_of_delays_carrier", "num_of_delays_security", "num_of_delays_late_aircraft", "Grand_total"
)

# display(Q2_wide)

Q2_long = Q2_wide.unpivot(
    index=["airport_code"],
    on=["Carrier_Proportion", "Security_Proportion", "Late_Aircraft_Proportion"],
    variable_name="Delay_Type",
    value_name="Proportion"
)

# display(Q2_long)

(
    ggplot(data=Q2_long, mapping=aes(x="airport_code", y="Proportion", fill="Delay_Type"))
    + geom_bar(stat="identity")

    + theme_gray()
)


```
